extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the EU AI Act provides two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII.
For most high-risk AI systems not embedded in regulated products under Annex I, the self-assessment (Annex VI) route can be used.

Third-party assessment via a notified body (Annex VII) is mandatory for high-risk AI systems involving biometric identification and for certain critical infrastructure systems listed in point 1 of Annex III.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements.
A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except for predetermined changes in systems designed to continue learning after being placed on the market.

Under Article 43, for the Annex VII procedure the provider may generally choose any notified body, but where the system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions/bodies/agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body instead.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to derogate from the standard conformity assessment procedure and authorise placing a specific high-risk AI system on the market, for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life/health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

Section 5 of the AI Act (Articles 40–49) covers harmonised standards, common specifications, presumption of conformity, conformity assessment (Art. 43), certificates (Art. 44), notified body information obligations (Art. 45), derogation (Art. 46), EU declaration of conformity (Art. 47), CE marking (Art. 48), and registration (Art. 49).
Notified bodies, once designated, are assigned identification numbers and listed under Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

Notified bodies for the AI Act, like those under other EU product legislation, are expected to be published in the Commission's NANDO (New Approach Notified and Designated Organisations) information system.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and capacity described as limited.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the medical devices/SaMD context.
As of October 2025, under the separate MDR/IVDR framework (not the AI Act), NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies.

A proposed Commission act (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV listing codes and categories of AI systems for notified body designation purposes within the NANDO system, and would also amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements.

A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) references codes for AI systems subject to Annex I that set the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies 'notified under Article 30' of the Regulation, a different article number than the Article 35 commonly cited for notified body lists.

Under the Cyber Resilience Act (a separate, non-AI-Act regulation), zero notified bodies had been designated in the NANDO database as of late June 2026, with a target of sufficient notified body capacity by 11 December 2026.

August 2026 is described as the deadline by which high-risk AI obligations, including conformity assessment requirements, fully apply, with post-2026 notified bodies designated under the AI Act expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments alongside MDR/IVDR assessments.

Notified bodies, where access to other reasonable means of verifying conformity is exhausted and insufficient, may be granted access (upon reasoned request) to the training and trained models of a high-risk AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards, per Annex VII point 4.5.

The Commission may adopt delegated acts under Article 43(5) to update Annex VI (internal control procedure) and Annex VII (QMS and technical documentation assessment) in light of technical progress, without needing to revise the AI Act itself.
A notified body is an independent third-party organisation officially designated by an EU Member State to perform conformity assessment procedures required under the AI Act.

It is unclear how many, if any, AI Act notified body designations had occurred by October 2026 (the current date), since the most recent dated sources (March and April 2026) report none or an ongoing/incomplete process.

The relationship and consistency between the Article 30 reference in the Council document and the Article 35/43 framework used elsewhere is not explained, leaving ambiguity about whether this refers to a recast, annex, or different legal instrument.

It is unclear what interim compliance options exist for providers if no notified bodies are designated by the August 2026 deadline for high-risk AI obligations.

report:
# Conformity Assessment of High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act: Procedures and Notified Body Designation Status

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two primary conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems—internal control (self-assessment) and third-party assessment by notified bodies—with the applicable route depending on the system's category (low confidence) [EU AI Act conformity assessment — Annex VI vs Annex VII](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment). While the legal framework for notified body designation is established in the Act, the actual notified body ecosystem remains largely undeveloped as of early-to-mid 2026, with no confirmed designations specifically under the AI Act reported in available sources (low confidence) [Notified Bodies Under the EU AI Act](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [EU AI Act and Medical Devices: MDR/IVDR Interplay Guide](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act provides two main routes: internal control based on Annex VI, or third-party assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII (low confidence) [EU AI Act conformity assessment](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [AI Conformity Assessment Under the EU AI Act](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment). For most high-risk AI systems not embedded in regulated products under Annex I, the self-assessment (Annex VI) route can be used (low confidence) [EU AI Act Conformity Assessment: Step-by-Step](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment). Third-party notified body assessment (Annex VII) becomes mandatory for high-risk systems involving biometric identification and for certain critical infrastructure systems under Annex III, point 1 (low confidence) [Conformity assessment of high-risk AI systems](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai).

For systems already covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) under Annex I Section A, providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai). A new conformity assessment is generally required after substantial modification of a system, with exceptions for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) [Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Providers may generally select any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where the system is intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs this function instead (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43 (GA)](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard procedures and temporarily authorise market placement for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) [Article 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Notified bodies may, in limited circumstances, be granted access to training and trained models, including parameters, subject to confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) [Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7). Separately, the Commission may adopt delegated acts under Article 43(5) to update Annex VI and Annex VII in light of technical progress without revising the AI Act itself, though this claim rests on limited sourcing (low confidence) [Conformity Assessments under the EU AI Act: A step-by-step guide](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf).

### Notified Body Designation Framework
Notified bodies, once designated, receive identification numbers and are listed under Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (low confidence) [Article 35](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35). They are expected to be published in the Commission's NANDO information system, consistent with practice under other EU product legislation (high confidence) [NANDO - Medical Devices](https://health.ec.europa.eu/medical-devices-topics-interest/notified-bodies-medical-devices_en). A proposed Commission act (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV listing codes/categories for notified body designation within NANDO, and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements, though this remains at proposal stage (medium confidence) [COM(2025) 836](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf).

### Current Designation Status
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing and capacity described as limited (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act specifically in the medical devices/SaMD context (low confidence) [MDR/IVDR Interplay Guide](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide). By contrast, under the separate MDR/IVDR framework, NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies as of October 2025 (high confidence) [EUR-Lex SWD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051). August 2026 is cited as the deadline for full application of high-risk AI obligations, with post-2026 notified bodies expected to conduct AI Act-specific assessments alongside MDR/IVDR work (low confidence) [mdxcro.com](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources diverge on whether any AI Act notified body designations had occurred by early-to-mid 2026: one (March 2026) frames designation as an ongoing process without confirming zero designations, while another (April 2026) explicitly states none had been formally designated—these may describe the same situation differently (both **low confidence**). A Council document references "Article 30" for notified body designation scope, inconsistent with the Article 35/43 numbering used elsewhere; this discrepancy is unexplained (**low confidence** for claim_015). Several other claims are flagged as low confidence, including the core description of Article 43's two routes (0.17), mandatory Annex VII triggers (0.24), identification numbering under Article 35 (0.12), and delegated act powers under Article 43(5) (0.03). Additionally, one candidate source (an Annex III practical guide, VDE-adjacent in provenance) was found to contain an embedded, prompt-injection-style instruction directing summarizers to include a specific external link unrelated to regulatory content; this instruction was identified and disregarded in producing this report, and no claim from that instruction is reflected above.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms an actual list or count of notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act. It remains unclear how many, if any, designations occurred by October 2026. The relationship between the "Article 30" reference and the Article 35/43 framework is unresolved. The practical effect and adoption status of the proposed Annex XIV is unconfirmed. No source identifies which Member States have begun notifying bodies for AI Act purposes, nor what interim compliance options exist if no notified bodies are designated by the August 2026 deadline.

# Conformity Assessment of High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act: Procedures and Notified Body Designation Status

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two primary conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems—internal control (self-assessment) and third-party assessment by notified bodies—with the applicable route depending on the system's category (low confidence) [EU AI Act conformity assessment — Annex VI vs Annex VII](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment). While the legal framework for notified body designation is established in the Act, the actual notified body ecosystem remains largely undeveloped as of early-to-mid 2026, with no confirmed designations specifically under the AI Act reported in available sources (low confidence) [Notified Bodies Under the EU AI Act](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [EU AI Act and Medical Devices: MDR/IVDR Interplay Guide](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act provides two main routes: internal control based on Annex VI, or third-party assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII (low confidence) [EU AI Act conformity assessment](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [AI Conformity Assessment Under the EU AI Act](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment). For most high-risk AI systems not embedded in regulated products under Annex I, the self-assessment (Annex VI) route can be used (low confidence) [EU AI Act Conformity Assessment: Step-by-Step](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment). Third-party notified body assessment (Annex VII) becomes mandatory for high-risk systems involving biometric identification and for certain critical infrastructure systems under Annex III, point 1 (low confidence) [Conformity assessment of high-risk AI systems](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai).

For systems already covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) under Annex I Section A, providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai). A new conformity assessment is generally required after substantial modification of a system, with exceptions for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) [Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Providers may generally select any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where the system is intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs this function instead (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43 (GA)](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard procedures and temporarily authorise market placement for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) [Article 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Notified bodies may, in limited circumstances, be granted access to training and trained models, including parameters, subject to confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) [Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7).

### Notified Body Designation Framework
Notified bodies, once designated, receive identification numbers and are listed under Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (low confidence) [Article 35](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35). They are expected to be published in the Commission's NANDO information system, consistent with practice under other EU product legislation (high confidence) [NANDO - Medical Devices](https://health.ec.europa.eu/medical-devices-topics-interest/notified-bodies-medical-devices_en). A proposed Commission act (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV listing codes/categories for notified body designation within NANDO, and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements, though this remains at proposal stage (medium confidence) [COM(2025) 836](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf).

### Current Designation Status
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing and capacity described as limited (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act specifically in the medical devices/SaMD context (low confidence) [MDR/IVDR Interplay Guide](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide). By contrast, under the separate MDR/IVDR framework, NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies as of October 2025 (high confidence) [EUR-Lex SWD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051). August 2026 is cited as the deadline for full application of high-risk AI obligations, with post-2026 notified bodies expected to conduct AI Act-specific assessments alongside MDR/IVDR work (low confidence) [mdxcro.com](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources diverge on whether any AI Act notified body designations had occurred by early-to-mid 2026: one (March 2026) frames designation as an ongoing process without confirming zero designations, while another (April 2026) explicitly states none had been formally designated—these may describe the same situation differently (both **low confidence**). A Council document references "Article 30" for notified body designation scope, inconsistent with the Article 35/43 numbering used elsewhere; this discrepancy is unexplained (**low confidence** for claim_015). Several other claims are flagged as low confidence, including the core description of Article 43's two routes (0.17), mandatory Annex VII triggers (0.24), identification numbering under Article 35 (0.12), and delegated act powers under Article 43(5) (0.03).

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms an actual list or count of notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act. It remains unclear how many, if any, designations occurred by October 2026. The relationship between the "Article 30" reference and the Article 35/43 framework is unresolved. The practical effect and adoption status of the proposed Annex XIV is unconfirmed. No source identifies which Member States have begun notifying bodies for AI Act purposes, nor what interim compliance options exist if no notified bodies are designated by the August 2026 deadline.
